summary: A 1934 pole lookout replaced by today's 53-ft R-6 tower in 1964; staffed each summer, drive-to above Libby, with roof and window restoration from 2019 to 2021.

facts.design: R-6 flat-cab treated-timber tower (present); first lookout a 50 ft pole tower with L-4 cab

staffing.status: staffed every summer (register, undated); still staffed in fire season (Western News, 2020)

access.note: Drive-to lookout above Libby; accessible seasonally by vehicle.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kootenai National Forest

events.note: First lookout: 50 ft pole tower with L-4 cab
Present 53 ft treated-timber tower with R-6 flat cab
New roof; the Forest Service covered the roof repair cost; association volunteers helped; completed early October
52 windows glazed; catwalk, railing and landing posts replaced; lookout scraped, sanded and painted

evidence.supports: first lookout 50 ft pole tower with L-4 cab in 1934; present tower replaced it
evidence.quote: Overlooking the town of Libby, the first lookout was a 50' pole tower with L-4 cab in 1934. This was replaced with the present 53' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab in 1964. It is staffed every summer.

evidence.supports: first lookout 50 ft pole tower with L-4 cab in 1934; present tower replaced it
evidence.quote: Overlooking the town of Libby, the first lookout was a 50' pole tower with L-4 cab in 1934. This was replaced with the present 53' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab in 1964.

evidence.supports: present tower 53 ft, R-6 flat cab, replaced in 1964
evidence.quote: This was replaced with the present 53' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab in 1964.
Swede Mountain lookout, a 52-foot, treated-timber tower, is accessible seasonally by vehicle.

evidence.supports: views of the Libby Valley, Kootenai River Valley and Cabinet Mountains Wilderness
evidence.quote: Visitors gain views of the Libby Valley, the Kootenai River Valley and the eastern front of the Cabinet Mountains Wilderness.

evidence.supports: new roof installed fall 2019 by a Kalispell roofing company with volunteers; still staffed in fire season
evidence.quote: Volunteers working alongside a roofing company from Kalispell installed a new roof this fall on the Swede Mountain lookout tower, sited a few miles east of Libby in the Kootenai National Forest and still staffed during fire season.

evidence.supports: Forest Service covered roof repair cost; completed early October
evidence.quote: Manning said the U.S. Forest Service covered the cost of the roof repairs and a group of the association's volunteers helped with the work, completed in early October.

evidence.supports: named among still-staffed Kootenai lookouts in 2020
evidence.quote: Among the remaining lookouts on the Kootenai National Forest that are still staffed are Swede Mountain, Marston and Black Butte.
In 2019 a new roof was put on and additional stabilizing of the roof in 2020.

evidence.supports: 52 windows glazed, catwalk and landing posts replaced, then scraped, sanded and painted
evidence.quote: The first part consisted of volunteers glazing 52 windows, replacing catwalk posts, railing, and landing posts. The second project consisted of scraping, sanding and painting the lookout.

evidence.supports: two 2021 projects; 52 windows glazed; landing posts replaced
evidence.quote: There were two projects at Big Swede on the Libby Ranger District this summer. In the first, 52(!) windows were glazed, the catwalk posts were replaced, and railings and posts were replaced on the 1st and 2nd landings.
Big Swede is a drive-to lookout overlooking the town of Libby.

corrections.why: 15.2 m is 50 ft, the height of the 1934 pole tower. The present tower is 53 ft, about 16.2 m. The 2020 Western News gives 52 ft.

corrections.proposed: 1934 built as the first lookout (50 ft pole tower); present tower built 1964
corrections.why: The register and FireLookout.com both say the 1934 tower was replaced by the present tower in 1964.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and FireLookout.com give 53 ft for the current tower. The 2020 Western News gives 52 ft. The story uses 53 ft and notes the difference.

sources.title: Looking out for Montana's fire lookouts

notes_for_editor: The record's 15.2 m height is the 1934 pole tower's 50 ft; see corrections. The record's 2020 'assessed' event ('One of four Libby District assessments that set the 2021 priorities') was not found in any page read, so it is left out. The 'NMLA board member' detail in the 2019 event was not verified and is left out. The 2020 Western News article says the Forest Service covered roof repair costs; the record's 'roofing firm' wording is supported by the same article. A Visit Montana listing appeared only in search results and was not used. Staffing 'as_of' is 2020 because the dated source is the 2020 article; the register and FireLookout.com pages are undated.
